items.key: desktop-ipc|restart crashed services automatically and alert me
items.title: Restart crashed services automatically and alert me
items.why: A service that crashes while StackConsole sits in the tray stays down until you happen to open the window; nothing restarts it and nothing tells you.
items.evidence: main.js:267 markExited sets status 'crashed' and stops; main.js:197 the tray only relabels its menu
items.benefit: Dev servers and queue workers recover from transient crashes; a native notification names the service and exit code when it doesn't.
items.drawbacks: A crash loop can spam restarts and notifications, so it needs a backoff and a 'give up after N' limit; another per-command setting.

items.key: forms|add environment variables per command and env files
items.title: Add environment variables per command (and .env files)
items.why: Commands only inherit StackConsole's own environment, so setting PORT, APP_ENV or a database URL per service means wrapping the command in shell tricks.
items.evidence: main.js:315 spawn env is { ...process.env, PYTHONUNBUFFERED } only; the command form has no env field (src/util/command-form.js)
items.benefit: Run the same app twice on different ports, switch .env.local / .env.testing per service, keep secrets out of the command line shown in the header.
items.drawbacks: Values may hold secrets: they must stay out of logs and the header, and projects.json then contains them in plain text.

items.key: crud|import commands from package json composer json and procfile
items.title: Import commands from package.json, composer.json and Procfile
items.why: A new project starts empty and every command is typed by hand, although the project folder already lists them (npm scripts, composer scripts, Procfile).
items.evidence: src/main.js:150 empty state only offers 'Add command' one at a time; add-project.html already asks for the project folder
items.benefit: Setting up a Laravel + Vite stack goes from four forms to one checklist; fewer typos in commands.
items.drawbacks: Needs a read-only file reader in main (path must stay inside the chosen folder); script names don't say which ones are long-running servers.

items.key: flows|start services in order wait until a dependency is ready
items.title: Start services in order: wait until a dependency is ready
items.why: Launch all starts everything at once and the only ordering tool is a fixed startup delay, so the API often starts before the database or Redis is listening.
items.evidence: main.js:308 startupDelay is a blind timer; main.js:413 cmd-launch-all starts every command at once; main.js:185 detectUrl already knows when a service is listening
items.benefit: Launch all becomes reliable; reuses the 'ready' signal (detected URL) the engine already has.
items.drawbacks: Dependency cycles must be prevented; services that never print a URL need another ready signal (a log line or a port check).

items.key: desktop-ipc|warn when a port is already taken and offer to free it
items.title: Warn when a port is already taken, and offer to free it
items.why: If :8000 is still held by an orphaned php or node process, the service just crashes with EADDRINUSE and you go hunting with netstat.
items.evidence: main.js:308 start path never checks the configured port before spawning
items.benefit: Shows who holds the port (process name + pid) before starting, with 'Stop that process' or 'Start anyway'.
items.drawbacks: Killing a process StackConsole didn't start is risky: needs a clear confirmation; port lookup differs per OS (netstat on Windows).

items.key: desktop-ipc|open a project or service folder in explorer vs code or a terminal
items.title: Open a project or service folder in Explorer, VS Code or a terminal
items.why: Folders are typed or browsed once and then disappear: to look at a service's code you leave StackConsole and dig through D:\projects by hand.
items.evidence: Folder paths only show in the Shell header and Project Manager (src/main.js renderShellHeader, project-manager.html); 34 runnable repos under D:\projects
items.benefit: One click from a running service to its code, its folder or a terminal already in the right directory (cwd = the service's working directory).
items.drawbacks: VS Code may not be installed or on PATH (fall back to Explorer); needs a small allow-listed IPC that only opens folders StackConsole knows.

items.key: desktop-ipc|relink a project whose folder moved e g c projects to d projects
items.title: Relink a project whose folder moved (e.g. C:\projects to D:\projects)
items.why: Two of your projects still point at C:\projects\… while the repos now live on D:\projects; StackConsole only says "Folder not found" when you press Start.
items.evidence: data/projects.json: Smartlab → C:\projects\Smartlab, asdasdsad → C:\projects\AI integrated projects\…\mobile (both missing); main.js executionEngineStart 'Folder not found'
items.benefit: A "Folder missing" badge with Find it… / Relink, plus an automatic suggestion when a folder with the same name exists elsewhere (D:\projects\AI integrated projects\smart-lab-inventory-report-system).
items.drawbacks: Auto-matching by name can pick the wrong copy; always confirm before relinking.

items.key: crud|keep a stack file in the repo stackconsole json so the setup travels with git
items.title: Keep a stack file in the repo (.stackconsole.json) so the setup travels with git
items.why: A project's commands live only in StackConsole's own data file; a new machine or a teammate rebuilds them by hand, like PM2's ecosystem file or Warp launch configs avoid.
items.evidence: Config is stored only in data/projects.json (main.js getDbPath); the import scan already reads repo files (main/importer.js)
items.benefit: Clone a repo, open it in StackConsole, and its services (commands, folders, ports, start order) appear; changes can be saved back to the file and reviewed in git.
items.drawbacks: Two sources of truth (file vs app) need a clear rule; secrets must never be written to the file.

items.key: flows|restore what was running when stackconsole quit
items.title: Restore what was running when StackConsole quit
items.why: After a reboot or a quit you start the same services again one by one; StackConsole forgets what you were running.
items.evidence: Runtime state is memory-only by design (Decision - Runtime state lives in memory); nothing records the last running set
items.benefit: On launch: "Restore 4 services from SmartLaboratory System?" with one click (respects start order).
items.drawbacks: Must ask, never auto-start silently; services may have been stopped on purpose.

items.key: forms|browse for a command s working directory and show its repo and git branch
items.title: Browse… for a command's working directory and show its repo and git branch
items.why: Services from several folders or repos already work (absolute working directories are allowed) but you have to type the path, and nothing shows which repo or branch a service runs from.
items.evidence: src/util/command-form.js InpDir is a plain text field; main.js executionEngineStart accepts absolute workingDirectory; your SmartLaboratory services use frontend / backend / ai subfolders
items.benefit: Cross-repo stacks become discoverable (automart: admin-api + admin-web + core-api); a branch label prevents "why is the old code running?".
items.drawbacks: Branch is read from .git/HEAD (no git binary needed) and can be stale until the next refresh.

items.key: crud|set up several repos at once from a checklist
items.title: Set up several repos at once from a checklist
items.why: D:\projects has 38 repos that aren't projects yet; Not set up handles them one click at a time, so a first run that wants ten projects takes ten trips down a long list.
items.evidence: QA on the real D:\projects 2026-10-07: Not set up (38); KI-010; concept A1 in .design-engine/work/master-folder-concepts.html
items.benefit: First run in one window: tick repos (with 1 project / N projects per container), see the command count, set them all up.
items.drawbacks: Another window; bulk setup can create projects you then archive.

items.key: general|switch focus with a scope rail and drill in instead of scrolling
items.title: Switch focus with a scope rail and drill-in instead of scrolling
items.why: With 45 repos and several master folders the tree gets long; focusing on one product (automart) means collapsing everything else by hand.
items.evidence: User asked for a more unique tree switcher than dropdowns (2026-10-07); edge cases for it listed in master-folder-parent-options.html#checklist
items.benefit: One click or Ctrl+1…9 to show one folder, with live badges on the rail so running services elsewhere stay visible.
items.drawbacks: About 40px of width at the 900px minimum; risk of 'where did my project go' if the scope is restored at launch.

items.key: general|find repos deeper than the scan depth look deeper here
items.title: Find repos deeper than the scan depth ("Look deeper here")
items.why: Discovery stops at folder → container → repo, so a repo in clients\acme\2024\app never shows in Not set up.
items.benefit: Deep layouts work without adding each subfolder as its own master folder.
items.drawbacks: Deeper scans cost more time; needs a per-folder setting.

items.key: general|jump to a project with ctrl19 the order of the iconsonly sidebar
items.title: Jump to a project with Ctrl+1–9 (the order of the icons-only sidebar)
items.why: Projects now have a tile and a fixed order in the rail; reaching the 4th one still needs the mouse or many arrow presses.
items.evidence: Concept C4 switcher (Ctrl+1–5) in .design-engine/work/redesign; renderRail() in src/main.js
items.benefit: Switch between the 2–3 projects you work on without leaving the keyboard.
items.drawbacks: Shortcuts must not clash with log find or text fields; order changes when projects are added.

items.key: general|filter and level chips for the second log too
items.title: Filter and level chips for the second log too
items.why: With two logs side by side, Ctrl+F, Warnings/Errors and Copy act on the main log only.
items.evidence: Decision - Workbench layout and identity (find acts on the main log); src/util/log-view.js has no finder
items.benefit: Hunt an error across api + web without swapping the panes.
items.drawbacks: Two find states to show; the toolbar must say which pane it targets.

items.key: general|remember a pair of logs per project eg adminapi beside adminweb
items.title: Remember a pair of logs per project (e.g. admin-api beside admin-web)
items.why: automart's API and web app are always watched together; the second log is set by hand each time you change project.
items.evidence: automart: 3 repos run together (Decision - Master folders); beside is one global per-viewer pref (sc.beside)
items.benefit: Selecting a project brings back the view you use for it.
items.drawbacks: Hidden state: the second pane appearing by itself can surprise; needs a visible 'remembered' cue.
